solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mean-spirited king has Russian runner sent back

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles

indicators.note: sent back means the river's name is written backwards after the king

parts.note: the Neva is the river through St Petersburg; a river 'runs'

explanation.surface: A petty monarch keeps returning a Russian athlete to his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but in crosswords a runner is often a river, here one flowing through St Petersburg.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly and contemptible, a fair synonym for mean-spirited behaviour.

clue.text: Box on the head becomes clichéd when old

definitions.note: a noun, a stale joke, defined by its usual phrase 'old chestnut'

parts.note: a chest is a box for storage
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A blow to the head turns into a tired joke over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box on the head' suggests a punch; it is a storage box followed by a slang word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a joke or story repeated so often it has become hackneyed.

clue.text: Make fine tea and eat nut fudge

indicators.note: to fudge is to fake or muddle, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Brew a nice tea and enjoy a nutty fudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fudge' looks like a sweet to eat, but it is the verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To attenuate is to make thin or slender, as fine thread is thin.

clue.text: Starts to exercise with esteemed Reds' pitcher

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A respected Reds baseball pitcher begins a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reds and pitcher suggest baseball; a pitcher is also a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug for water, a pitcher in the other sense.

clue.text: Omit expressions of approval for items of sports equipment

parts.note: to skip something is to leave it out
olés are cheers of approval, as at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Someone skips the cheering and talks about kit for sport instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski poles are the sticks a skier carries, pieces of equipment for a winter sport.

clue.text: Want to penetrate stronghold being very much involved

indicators.note: to penetrate means the want word goes inside the stronghold word

parts.note: a keep is a castle's central tower
to want is to need

explanation.surface: A craving to storm a fortress while deeply caught up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee-deep in something means heavily engaged or immersed in it.

clue.text: To get rid of inside left is a help for defenders

indicators.note: inside means the removal word goes within the left word joined to 'is'

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
to cull is to remove selectively

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the inside left, a football position, helps the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside left' reads as a football position, but 'inside' is the insertion signal and 'left' is the nautical side.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is a heavy grille dropped over a castle gate to keep attackers out.

clue.text: Henry and others covering up for Turner

indicators.note: covering means the reversed words wrap around the Henry letter
up in a down clue means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for 'and others'
H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry and his friends cover up for the painter Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns ETAL into LATE, which by 'covering' holds H. Turner looks like the painter J.M.W. Turner but means a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that rotates wood or metal while it is shaped, so it turns things.

clue.text: Back for a short time

definitions.meaning: ... meaning: a moment, as in 'wait a ...'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back for a short time' sounds like a brief return; the two stretches are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for supporting a proposal and a noun for a brief moment.

clue.text: Half-hearted roar coming from downstairs

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the pair of central letters is dropped, halving the heart

parts.note: a bellow is a loud roar

explanation.surface: A feeble shout heard from the floor beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Below means on a lower floor, so downstairs is a fair equivalent.

clue.text: Great old rock band overwhelmed by endless support

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the band sits inside the shortened support word
endless means the final letter of the support word is cut off

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball
R.E.M. is an American rock band

explanation.surface: A veteran rock group is swamped by a support act that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Extreme was itself a rock band, so the clue tempts you to read the band as the answer's source rather than as a pointer to a different group.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme describes something of the highest degree, as does great in 'great danger'.

clue.text: Unpredictable informer hiding in Morecambe

indicators.note: hiding in means the informer word is tucked inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe, the British comedian of Morecambe and Wise
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: A shifty informant lies low in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort, but it stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe, half of a famous British TV double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is irregular and inconsistent, so it cannot be predicted.

clue.text: Son leaving was thoroughly abhorrent in defeat

indicators.note: leaving means the son's letter departs from the word

parts.note: stank, as in 'the whole affair stank'
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son walks out, disgusted by how badly a defeat was handled.
explanation.definitionFit: To tank is informal for losing heavily, or beating a rival soundly, in a contest.

clue.text: Means of access from the east to conceal part of church

indicators.note: read from the east, that is right to left, the access word comes backwards

parts.note: a door gives access to a room
to screen something is to hide it

explanation.surface: Someone enters from the east to hide away a section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood screen is the carved partition between nave and chancel in many old churches.

clue.text: Philosopher after commencement dealt with being wronged

indicators.note: after commencement means only what follows the first letter is kept

parts.note: John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher
treated means handled, dealt with

explanation.surface: A philosopher, once things began, was handled harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-treated means abused or treated badly, so wronged.

clue.text: Incompetent foreign article on murder victim by the sound of it

parts.note: un is French for 'a'

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the victim's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: A clumsy foreign report about a murder victim, judging by what's heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to do a job lacks the skill for it, so is incompetent.

clue.text: Get to make concrete

definitions.meaning: first meaning: understand, as in 'I get it'
second meaning: bring into reality, as in realising a plan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make concrete' sounds like building work, but it means turn an idea into reality.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both grasping a fact mentally and converting an asset or plan into something actual.

clue.text: Winger magnificent before championship game

indicators.note: before places the magnificent word ahead of the winged creature

parts.note: superb means magnificent
an owl has wings, so it is a winger

explanation.surface: A brilliant winger shines ahead of the big final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a football player; here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the annual title game of American football's NFL.

clue.text: Not bound to prevail say without restraint

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for the noun, as in 'given free rein'

parts.note: free means not tied up

indicators.note: say means the ruling word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to reign is to prevail or hold sway

explanation.surface: Unshackled and ready to win, acting with no limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Free rein is complete freedom of action, a loosened bridle on a horse.

clue.text: Banter with soldiers and leave Peter oddly neglected

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
to part is to leave

indicators.note: oddly neglected means the odd-placed letters are ignored, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Soldiers swap jokes and depart, ignoring Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty exchange in conversation, which is banter.

clue.text: Exploit river mouth perhaps

parts.note: an exploit is a daring deed, a feat
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of where a river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a verb and 'river mouth' as one phrase; in fact the noun exploit gives FEAT, and the mouth is a face's.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth is an example of a facial feature, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Spot somewhat sharp implement

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Noticing something rather like a pointed tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot on the skin is a small inflamed blemish, the same thing.

clue.text: Cringe around Poland's foremost poet

indicators.note: around means the cringing word wraps the letter

parts.note: to cower is to cringe in fear

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A poet shrinks back before Poland's leading figure.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper was an 18th-century English poet and hymn writer.

clue.text: Reluctant to delete a piece of poetry

indicators.note: to delete says the next letter must be taken out

parts.note: averse means unwilling

explanation.surface: Unwilling to cut a passage from a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse is a stanza or line of a poem, a piece of it.

clue.text: Kind of Hell with Eve not being truthful

indicators.note: kind of means the letters are made into a version of themselves, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sort of hell shared with Eve, lacking honesty — a biblical fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the level is an idiom for being honest and straightforward.

clue.text: Nets, split from the bottom, ultimately useless

indicators.note: from the bottom in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: to part is to split

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Torn nets, ripped from below, end up useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps and nets are both devices for catching animals.

clue.text: Girl missing the first song

indicators.note: missing the first means the name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl skips the opening number of a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Apparent in zombie rising from coffin carrier

indicators.note: Apparent in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A zombie climbing out of its coffin, horror-film style.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'from' into the definition; it is a link word, and the definition is 'coffin carrier'. 'Rising' is part of the hidden text, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the stand on which a coffin is placed or carried to the grave.

clue.text: Former PM not entirely following priest's foolish talk

indicators.note: following places the shortened name after the priest's letters

parts.note: PR is an abbreviation for priest

indicators.note: not entirely means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee, British Prime Minister 1945-51

explanation.surface: A former prime minister partly echoing a cleric's silly chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee led Britain's post-war Labour government; 'not entirely' drops his final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prattle is idle, childish chatter, talk with no sense to it.

clue.text: Hold forth about batting and keep going

indicators.note: about means the talking word goes around the batting word

parts.note: to spout is to talk at length
a cricket side batting is 'in'

explanation.surface: Someone lectures on cricket and refuses to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out a task is to prolong it, making it last longer.

clue.text: Inherent in dirt seen all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something intrinsic to the grime spotted everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality resident in something is present within it by nature, a synonym for inherent.

clue.text: If not, then gold instead

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
else means otherwise, instead

explanation.surface: A choice: take this, or else have gold instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Or else introduces the consequence of failing, meaning otherwise.
